title: Get READI plan and fire safety box by-law
subtitle: Also: customer service standards, Official Plan review public meeting on parking and commercial uses, volunteerism delegation.
overview: Council received the draft Get READI plan, the city's first reconciliation, equity, accessibility, diversity and inclusion plan, for information {{vote:m3}}. Staff said the final plan returns to Council in December, a first implementation plan follows early next year, and an update on grant processes for cultural groups could come as early as January 2025.

Council also approved a Customer Service Standards Policy, to be presented to all staff in fall 2024 {{vote:m2}}, and a new Fire Safety Box By-law with matching changes to the administrative penalty by-law {{vote:m4}}. Council then enacted those by-laws along with a zoning by-law amendment for 20 University Avenue East, which had been considered at the September 9 meeting {{vote:m5}}.

In the evening, Council held a statutory public meeting on phase one of the Official Plan Review. No decisions were made. Staff will review the comments and bring a recommended plan back, with early December as the target. Earlier, a delegation from Volunteer Waterloo Region described declining formal volunteering and asked Council to keep supporting it.

decisions.detail: Council approved the Fire Safety Box By-law and the related amendment to the General Administrative Penalty By-Law 2023-038.
Council received the draft plan for information, with the final plan expected in December and an implementation plan in early 2025.
Council approved the policy and directed the Chief Administrative Officer or designate to present it to all staff in fall 2024.

debate: On Get READI, one councillor asked how cultural groups will find grant funding. Staff said a gap exists, was covered in 2024 from team and commissioner budgets, and that the team will apply an equity lens to existing grants rather than run its own.

Councillors asked that the plan address poverty, neurodivergence, attitudes toward people in public spaces and all ages. Staff said these appeared in consultations in other words, such as housing, low-cost space and sensory-friendly events, and the implementation plan will use an intersectional lens.
Another councillor asked about data practices, staff retention and indicators. Staff said community input should shape how data is collected and how success is measured.

At the Official Plan public meeting, student delegates and residents urged removing parking minimums citywide, citing housing and rent costs. Staff said the Official Plan sets direction while zoning sets parking numbers.

Other speakers asked for more commercial uses in suburbs and raised concerns about emissions, transit access and the five-storey limit in Uptown. A planner for a property owner asked for a mixed-use designation on Weber Street, and staff said some larger-format commercial land is still needed.
